bull.b: A debt-free balance sheet reduces borrowing-related financial risk and preserves flexibility for clinical development. Without scheduled principal or interest obligations, Coya has greater scope to direct available resources toward its pipeline and manage uncertainty in a clinical-stage business.

The sharp increase in reported revenue demonstrates meaningful recent top-line momentum and indicates that Coya has generated substantial commercial or partnership-related inflows. If maintained, this growth could broaden funding capacity and support continued investment in its therapeutic programs.

The open-label extension builds on a fully enrolled Phase 2/3 ALS study and can provide additional long-term efficacy and safety information. This strengthens the evidence base around COYA 302 and supports clearer future development decisions as the program approaches its data readout.

bear.b: Extremely negative operating results show that the current business is not generating a sustainable earnings profile despite recent revenue growth. Persistent losses can restrict internal reinvestment, increase reliance on external funding, and make future development economics highly dependent on clinical success.

Consistently negative operating and free cash flow indicates that Coya consumes cash while advancing its programs rather than funding them internally. Continued burn creates ongoing financing needs and may pressure strategic choices if development spending remains high relative to available resources.

Deferring the FTD Phase 2 trial concentrates near-term resources and clinical optionality on ALS, reducing the pace at which Coya can diversify its pipeline evidence. A narrower near-term development focus also leaves progress more dependent on outcomes from the ALSTARS program.
